fieldMarks: Grey coat sprinkled with black and brown (sometimes red); paler underside; white tail underside
Smaller ears and shorter legs than hares
behavior: Social; lives in warrens (tunnel systems) with dominance hierarchies
Signals danger by thumping hind legs
Grazes grasses and leaves; re-ingests soft droppings
habitat: Dry areas with soft, sandy soil suitable for burrowing: grasslands, forest edges and cultivated land.
range: Native to the Iberian Peninsula and Mediterranean; introduced worldwide, including established populations in North America.

lookalikes.name: European hare
lookalikes.howToTell: Hares have longer ears and legs and do not live in warrens.
